transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump is returning from a historic trilateral summit in Asia with the presidents
of China, his host, and Russia.
This as Russia leader Vladimir Putin threatens revenge for Ukraine's bombing of a bridge
linking Russia's mainland to the annex Crimean Peninsula, and PR's Charles Mainz has details
from Moscow.
The 12-mile Kerch Bridge from Russia to Crimea has always been a symbol of Russia's claim
to the peninsula, Moscow illegally annexed from Ukraine in 2014, and a pet project of
the Russian presidents.
For that reason, Ukraine has repeatedly targeted the structure, including several missile attacks
this week that sent a section of road tumbling into the sea.
Addressing the media following his meetings with Presidents Trump and Xi, Putin acknowledged
serious damage to the bridge, but vowed Russia's response would be even more painful.
Putin also claimed at the time the bridge was struck, he'd been on the verge of agreeing
to a ceasefire with Ukraine on energy and maritime targets.
That deal, said Putin, was no longer on offer.
Charles Mainz, NPR News, Moscow.
The International Court of Justice says Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim
minority during the 2017 crackdown in Rakhine State.
It's the first time the United Nations' highest court has found a country responsible for
genocide.
A State Department spokesperson says the U.S. is reviewing the implications of the findings
from the ICJ.
The ruling is legally binding, but the court has no way to enforce it.
Torrential rain is flooding cities in California and Florida, as the country heads into a busy
holiday travel week, here's NPR's Ava Berger.
Social media is filled with images of flooded homes, underwater streets, and it's not
just in one U.S. city.
Palm Bay and Broward, Florida, as well as San Francisco, California, are just three
cities dealing with massive waves, historic rainfall, and seemingly never-ending storms.
This year, Super El Nino is making that wet weather more likely.
As for travel, it's too early to know exactly how Thanksgiving week will look.
But Jeff Baradelli, a chief meteorologist at WFLA-TV in Tampa Bay, says more storms
are expected through the weekend and next week on the East Coast.
It doesn't look like it's going to be an easy week for travel.
AAA says about 81 million Americans will be traveling next week.
Ava Berger, NPR News.
The AI giant anthropics debuted on the NASDAQ at $111.50 a share, about 30 percent above
its $83 IPO price, giving it an initial valuation of $1.5 trillion before ringing the opening
bell today.
CEO Daria Amade read a statement.
There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety
versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety.
And an obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into anthropics DNA from the
start.
It's NPR.
An Illinois man accused of plotting a mass shooting at a Chicago area Hindu temple last
month pleaded not guilty in court today to terrorism and other charges.
Police say 19-year-old Alexandros Paparakis was on the verge of carrying out an attack
outside the temple in Aurora, but his gun jammed.
He said a search of his house turned up a rifle, ammunition and a patch displaying imagery
associated with white supremacist extremism.
FIFA president Gianni Infantino will face two challengers in the upcoming election to head
the world's soccer body.
But as NPR's Rafael Nam tells us, Infantino appears well-placed to win another term.
The president of the French Football Federation, Philippe Diallo and Japanese soccer official
Kozo Tashima are officially running in the FIFA elections scheduled for mid-March.
By the tally by the Associated Press, shows Infantino is only a vote short of the threshold
needed to be re-elected, based on endorsements from soccer federations around the world.
It's a remarkable comeback after Infantino sparked major controversy after working on
a secret plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.
FIFA quickly abandoned the proposal and has been traveling around the world to make amends.
Rafael Nam, NPR News.
Grand Theft Auto VI made a major debut today.
The series' latest installment dropped at midnight, local time around the globe.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.

topics.text: President Trump returns from Asia summit with Chinese and Russian presidents
Putin vows painful response after Ukraine strikes damage Kerch Bridge to Crimea
International Court of Justice finds Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya in 2017
Torrential rain floods cities in California and Florida ahead of Thanksgiving travel
AI company Anthropic debuts on NASDAQ at $111.50 a share, valued at $1.5 trillion
Illinois man pleads not guilty to terrorism charges over plotted Aurora Hindu temple shooting
FIFA president Gianni Infantino faces two challengers in March election
Grand Theft Auto VI releases worldwide at midnight local time
